summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gangzhun studied at Qinghai Nationalities University until 1989. He earned a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University from 1998 to 2001 under the supervision of Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir studied at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) for an M.Phil under Hanna Havnevik, and also studied under the traditional teacher Lama Byambaa (attested 2008).
Active in the fields of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Garab Dorje Rinpoche received traditional training under teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

A scholar in Indology and linguistics, Garcin de Tassy studied at the Collège de France under Jean-Daniel Kieffer and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held a chair at École des Langues Orientales (circa 1828–1878) and directed the Société Asiatique (circa 1876–1878).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, Gareth Fisher completed a Ph.D. at the University of Virginia in 2006. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Gareth Sparham earned his Ph.D. at the University of British Columbia under Ashok Aklujkar (~1983–1989). He taught Tibetan at the University of Michigan (1999–2009) and held posts at UBC and UC Berkeley.

Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1972–1979). He served on the faculty at Harvard (~1979–1999), taught Sanskrit at Columbia (~1999–2007), and joined the University of Chicago around 2007.

Active in religious studies and philosophy, Gary D. DeAngelis studied under mentors Masatoshi Nagatomi and W. J. Johnson. As of 2017, he served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at the College of the Holy Cross.

A scholar in religious and Buddhist studies, Gary Snyder studied at Reed College, UC Berkeley under Shih-Hsiang Chen, and with several traditional teachers. He served as a professor at UC Davis from 1986 to 2002.

Gary Urton completed his Ph.D. in anthropology at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1979. He taught at Colgate University (1978–2002) and served as Dumbarton Oaks Professor of Pre-Columbian Studies at Harvard University (2012–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio studied at the University of Turin and under Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He held the chair in Sanskrit at the University of Turin (1852) and served as librarian and director at the National University Library of Turin (1859–1862).

A linguist who studied under Friedrich Christian Diez and at the École des chartes, Gaston Paris held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1903) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau worked in the fields of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at the École Polytechnique from approximately 1899 to 1901.
Gaton Ngawang Lekpa was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his studies under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

An Indology and religious studies scholar, Gauri Viswanathan studied at the University of Delhi and earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University in 1985. She taught English at Delhi (~1973–1978) before becoming a professor at Columbia (~1989).

An Indologist and philosopher, Gaurinath Sastri served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (~1957–1968) and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1976–1979). He was also Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society (attested 1959).

Gavin D'Costa, a religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Cambridge and the University of Birmingham. He taught at the West London Institute of Higher Education (~1985–1988) and became Emeritus Professor of Catholic Theology at the University of Bristol (1993).

Indologist Gavin Flood studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held posts at the University of Wales, Lampeter, University of Stirling, and was Professor of Hindu Studies and Comparative Religion at Oxford (2005–2015).

Gelek is a Tibetologist who served as a Researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998). He has also been a visiting lecturer at the University of California and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gelek Rinpoche achieved the Geshe Lharampa degree at Drepung Monastery, studied under masters such as Ling Rinpoche, and attended Cornell University. He served as director of Tibet House, New Delhi in 1965.
